pk.context: 10 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Absolute oral bioavailability is 78%, and a high-fat meal does not alter total exposure. About 91% is protein bound, and the drug and its related metabolites are mainly eliminated by the kidneys.
clues.substance: Supplied as a hydrated 1:1:1 complex; the active moiety has molecular weight 408.9.
clues.product: Marketed under an NDA in 5 mg and 10 mg strengths.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated after serious hypersensitivity to it or its excipients; anaphylaxis and angioedema have been reported.
clues.indication: Chronic kidney disease at risk of progression, heart failure, and type 2 diabetes with cardiovascular disease, plus glycemic control in type 2 diabetes.
clues.mechanism: Inhibits SGLT2 in the proximal renal tubules, reducing glucose reabsorption and promoting urinary glucose excretion.

tell: Cleared mainly by UGT1A9 to an inactive 3-O-glucuronide that accounts for 61% of a dose.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: the maximum plasma concentration (C max ) is usually attained within 2 hours under fasting state
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The mean plasma terminal half-life (t ½ ) for dapagliflozin is approximately 12.9 hours following a single oral dose of FARXIGA 10 mg
evidence.pill: 10 mg, yellow, biconvex, diamond-shaped, film-coated tablets
clues.kinetics: The absolute oral bioavailability of dapagliflozin following the administration of a 10 mg dose is 78%
does not alter AUC as compared with the fasted state
Dapagliflozin and related metabolites are primarily eliminated via the renal pathway
clues.safety: contraindicated in patients with a history of a serious hypersensitivity reaction to dapagliflozin or any of the excipients in FARXIGA
Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema have been reported with FARXIGA
clues.indication: in adults with chronic kidney disease at risk of progression
in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and either established CV disease or multiple CV risk factors
to improve glycemic control in adults and pediatric patients aged 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus
clues.mechanism: Dapagliflozin is an inhibitor of SGLT2
expressed in the proximal renal tubules
By inhibiting SGLT2, dapagliflozin reduces reabsorption of filtered glucose and thereby promotes urinary glucose excretion
